full_judgment:
2. Facts in short arc that the opposite party,	Md. Maftabuddin Chowdhury instituted a suit being.	Title Suit No. 586 of 1983 for ejectment of a tenant alleging, inter alia, that the defendant, namely, Messrs.’ National Tuberculosis Relief and Rehabilitation Society of Bangladesh was inducted in as a monthly tenant by the plaintiff landlord in respect of the suit premises being holding No. 98, New Elephant Road, Dhaka, as per terms and conditions of the contract. The tenancy was for a period of one year upto 14th March, 1982 with effect from 13th March, 1981. According to the terms of the agreement the rent was payable within 1st week of every month according to English Calendar month. The defendant paid rent very irregularly and not according to the terms of the contract and also over stayed in the premises. The plaintiff requested the defendant in writing to vacate the suit premises after the expiry of the lease but the defendant did not comply. The defendant tenant informed the plaintiff that it would not be possible for them to vacate it before December, 1982 and on that they were allowed to continue till December, 1982. During that period the defendant did not pay rent according to the terms of the agreement but very irregularly. After the expiry of December, 1982 the plaintiff requested the defendant again to vacate but to no result and lastly the plaintiff landlord served a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, but also to no result. Hence the suit for ejectment of the defendant from the suit premises 

 3. The suit was contested by the defendant by filing a written statement in which the material allegations made in the plaint had been denied. It is the case of the defendant that the defendant, which is a voluntary social welfare organization, paid the rent regularly to the plaintiff but the plaintiff was in the habit of taking rent in crossed cheese for 2/3 months at a time and the defendant paid rent for the months of September, and October, 1982 on 19.11.82 and also for November and December, 19R2 where after the landlord refused to take rent and lastly the defendant deposited the rent for the month of May and June, 1983 and July, August and September, 1983in the court, It has been stated that the defendant is not a defaulter and the suit is barred by waiver and acquiescence and they cannot be termed as a defaulter because of his own conduct. It has been also stated that the plaintiff never require the premises for his bona fide requirement as he has already constructed more shops and had rented out those to others at a higher rent and in fact, it is adopted as a device to throw out this social voluntary organisation from the premises only to induct new tenants with enhanced rent and salami. 

 5. The matter went on appeal where it was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka. The Court of appeal below after hearing both the parties dismissed the appeal on contest on a finding that a tenant making payment of rent in a lump is not protected. from eviction unless there is contract to the contrary or such payment is covered by waiver and acquiescence on the part of the landlord and on a finding that this payment of rent for 2/3/ months at a time having not been paid at a time on the basis of contract the defendant is a defaulter. The Court also found that the house is also required for the bonafide requirement of the plaintiff who is a retired Government servant and on these finding appeal was dismissed. The judgment and decree passed by the learned Munsif was affirmed. Against that judgment of affirmance this provisional application was moved and the Rule obtained from this Court on 12.11.1985 which is heard and disposed of by this judgment. 

 6. Mr. Md. Nawab A1i, learned Advocate endearing in support of the Rule having taken me through the impugned .judgment and the relevant papers and documents on record submitted that in spite of the fact that the petitioner as poreverhel understanding with the plaintiff had paid rents for 2/3months at a time with the consent and bona fide of the plaintiff and having regard to the fact that the fact plaintiff realised rent from the defendant uptoupto April, 1983 much alter the original lease agreement had expired, the courts below erred in has in holding that the petitioner organisation was a defaulter. It has been submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the defendant organisation was never a defaulter :1I1d the rent W33 always pad by cheque as mutually agreed upon C}I the parties. Lastly, it was submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the courts below without any basis came to a finding that the premises is required bona fide by the plaintiff, for his own purposes. 

 7. Mr. SharifuddinChakladar, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff opposite party on the other hand submitted that the courts below committed no error of law occasioning failure of justice in arriving at a finding to the effect that the defendant-tenant is a defaulter within the meaning of the provision of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, therefore. the petitioner is liable to be ejected outright and this concurrent finding of fact to the effect that the defendant was a defaulter, having found on the basis of evidence on record, need not be interfered with by this Court in exercise of its provisional jurisdiction. Mr. Chakladar further submitted that the plaintiff is a retired Government servant and he needs the premises for his own purposes and it was rightly found so by the courts below. He has referred to a number of decisions in support of the contortion to which I shall advert at the relevant portion of the judgment. 

 8. In the instant case certain facts arc admitted, namely, that the defendant organisation was inducted in as a tenant under a written agreement; that the tenancy was to continue from 13th March, 1981 to 14th March, 1982. It is in the agreement that alter 14th March, 1982 the lease will automatically terminate unless fresh agreement is made before that date with the agreement of both the parties, As to the mode of payment of rent it 'N~\S stipulated that the payment of rental will start from 15th day of march 1981 and shall be paid monthly for every' month within the 1st week of the following month according to English Calendar year It was also provided ,hat the payment will normally be made either at the demised premises or at the residence of the lessor, all bill and other communications will be handed over by the lessor to the man of the lessee. It has been further provided that if the lessee fails to pay rent within the following month he shall be liable to ejectment and no plea; whatsoever shall be maintainable in any court of law or elsewhere. 

 3. This agreement of lease appears to be very carefully drafted and signed by the respective parties in presence of two witnesses on a Tk.3/- non judicial stamp paper. It is also not disputed that after the expiry of the lease the plaintiff opposite party informed the defendant petitioner that they should vacate the premises. It is also not disputed that thereafter the parties sat in a compromise meeting at the house of Dr. Nurul Islam, and it was decided there that the defendant organisation would continue as tenant on an enhanced rent of Tk. 1500/- per month, all other conditions, remaining the same, till December, 1982 and the organisation remained there as tenant till December, 1982 but continued to remain thereafter, in the said premises till to-day. 

 10. The question that calls for determination in a matter like this is whether a tenant who was inducted in-as a 'tenant by the landlord, in a given case, would have the protection of the provision of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance against eviction. Section 18 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance provides that no order or decree for recovery of possession of any premises shall be made as long as the tenant pays rent to the full extent and performs the conditions of tenancy but no tenant shall be entitled to the benefit of section 18 unless he pays rent due by him in respect of such premises within the time fixed in the contract with the landlord and or in the absence of any such contract by the 15th day of the month next following that for which the rent is payable. Section 19 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance provides that when a landlord refuses to acceptany such rent remitted by the postal money order by a tenant the tenant may deposit such rent within a fortnight of the date of which the rent so remitted is returned to the tenant by the postal authorities as undelivered with the House Rent Controller and on such deposit the House Rent Controller within 15 days of the date of deposit forwarded the same by postal money order to the address of the landlord. Section 20 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance provides that withdrawal of any rent from the Controller by the landlord shall not in any way be used as an evidence that he has waived any notice to quit given by him to the tenant. 

 11. From a reading of these provisions along with the decided cases it appears that it has been consistently held by our courts that a person who fails to pay rent within the time fixed in the absence of such contract by the 15th of the month next following'that for which rent is payable, would be a defaulterand hence, shall not be entitled to the benefit of section 18 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance. In the instant case it appears from the pleadings of the plaint that the plaintiff opposite party did receive rentby crossed cheque for 2/3 months together. It has been clearly stated by the defendant petitioner in their written statement in Title Suit No. 586 of 1983 that the defendant used to pay the rent to the plaintiff opposite party when become due by cross cheque and it was the habit of the plaintiff to receive cross cheque for the rent of 2/3 months together and they paid rent for the month of May, 1983 on 8.6.83 but returned  back on 8.6.83. Again the defendant paid rent. for the month.of May and June, 1983 by crossed cheque on 5.7.83 which was also refused. The defendant again sent the rent for the month of May, June and July, 1983 on 3.8.83 but it was refused and returned back on 10.8.83 and the defendant, therefore, seek the protection of law and have been depositing the rent in the court of the House Rent Controller, Dhaka regularly in House Rent Case No. 481 of 1983 and it has been further stated in their written statement that the defendant is not a defaulter as alleged 

 12. From Ext. ' I ' which is a chalan, filed before the House Rent Controller showing payment of rent by the defendant petitioner for the month of May and June, 1983 by depositing on 3.11.83. From Ext.1(1) , it is seen that before the House Rent Controller again rents for the month of July, August and September, 1983 was deposited on 8.1l.83 when according to the defendant the rents for May, June and July, 1983 was refused and returned back to him on 10.8.83. Rent for the month of October was deposited on 14.1l.83. Rent for the month of November, 1983 was deposited on 13.12.83. Rent for the month of December, 1983 was deposited on 15.1.84 and for the month of January, 1984 was deposited on 14.2.84. 

 13. It thus, appears that nowhere rents have not been paid within the 15th day of the next month for which the rent was payable and due. There is also no dispute as to that fact as it is the case of the defendant petitioner that the landlord was in the habit of taking rent in a lump and therefore, he would be barred by waiver to object to that now and the learned lawyer for the opposite party referred to the decision reported in 31 D.L.R. (A.D.) 183 in support of that. Now even considering that it is a case of waiver so far the landlord is concerned the fact remains that even before the House Rent Controller rents were paid in lump and there cannot be any waiver by the House Rent Controller. 

 14. Certain decisions have been referred to by the lawyers at the Bar in this regard to which I shall advert now. In the case of M/s. Abdul Hoque V s. Zakir Hossain, reported in 1984 B.L.D.(A.D) 298, the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court had occasion to examine a similar point. In that case under report the case of the defendant was that the plaintiff used to collect rent for several months together and grant receipt ante dating them month-wise and the defendant never failed to pay rent to the representative of the respondent when they came to collect the rent. In that case the question thus, was whether admitted acceptance of rent in lump would be an evidence of a contract between the parties waiving the receipt to receive rent within 15 days following month for which the rent has become due and even if it does amount to a contract whether sub-section 5 of section 18 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance contemplated such kind of contract or agreement. Inreply to this their Lordships observed on a reference to the provisions of this sub-section(5) of section 18 that there the expression used was "within the time fixed in the contract or by the 15th day of the month next following that for which the rent is payable" Their Lordships also held that from the use of the preposition 'in' before the expression "the contract" the intention of the legislature seems to be clear. There might have been some scope for controversy if the preposition "by" was used instead of the preposition 'in'. Their Lordships held that the contract referred to here in this sub-section means a written contract and not an oral contract. 

 15. In the instant case there is no written contract varying the terms of the agreement which provided that the rents are to be paid within 15th of the next month and in its absence it cannot be said that the right of the landlord to demand rent in strict compliance within the agreement had been taken away. In the instant case it appears that the tenants had not only been irregular in paying rent to the landlord but had not even complied with the provision of law as to the deposit of rent with the House Rent Controller after the refusal by the landlord. 

 16. In the case of Ramjan Ali Misty Vs. Md. Hadeyetullah, reported in 31 D.L.R.(A.D.) 183 their Lordships of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh had finally spelt out the interpretation of the expression defaulter as in the section 18(5) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, 1983, both in the case of payment of rent to the landlord and deposit of rent before the House Rent Controller. It has been observed therein that the tenant must pay rent in terms of the contract and if the landlord refuses to accept rent the tenant must remit the rent within the aforesaid 15 days of the following month by money order. If the money order is refused he would deposit the rent with the House Rent Controller within a fortnight from the date of receipt of the undelivered rent, sent through the postal authority, and when these conditions are fulfilled by the tenant he gets the protection otherwise he becomes a defaulter and the protection from ejectment granted by the Ordinance is clearly taken away by the expressed language of sub-section 5 of section 18 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance. 

 17. In the case of P.K. Chakraborty Vs. A.P. Chowdhury and others reported in B.L.D. 1981 (A.D.) 19 their Lordships quoted with approval their decision in Ramjan Ali Mistry's case and held in the relevant portion thus: "Apart from this, it is to be observed that from Flagon, 1375 B.S. to the filing of the suit, the tenant attempted to deposit rent with the Rent Controller, but it appears that he had deposited rent once for three months at a time by Ext. A covering Chaitra, Baisakh, Jaistha and then again for two months by Ext. A(3) covering Bhadra and Aswan. These payments of rent clearly are not in compliance of the section 19 of the Ordinance and comes within the Rule of default as set out in Ramjan Ali's case". 

 18. Now coming to the instant case it is seen that there existed no written agreement subsequent to the original agreement, obliging the party to pay rent in lump, deviating from the stipulation contained in the original contract as to payment of rent within 15 of the next month and there is no written agreement also obliging the parties to accept rent in lump during the period from April, 1982 to December, 1982 which period admittedly was without any written agreement. In the absence of any written agreement under the Provision of law, rent is to be paid within 15th of the next month regularly. It is further seen from the record that the alleged refusal of the subsequent remittance of rent sent by the crossed cheer through post also speaks of a payment of rent in lump. Deposit of rent with the Rent Controller also speaks of payment of rent in lump. All these clearly takes away the protection of law as under the Premises Rent Control Ordinance from being evicted and hence, it has been rightly found by the courts below concurrently that the petitioner was a defaulter. This concurrent finding of fact having been found by the courts below causing no error of law either by a misreading of the evidence on record or by taking a wrong view of the law, I find nothing to interfere with the same in this Provisional jurisdiction of this court
